subject: [PATCH for-7.5 0/5] memcg: clean up memory.high enforcement

reviews.author: Harry Yoo
reviews.summary: Identified a missing Signed-off-by: line in the first patch and suggested adding it. Otherwise, LGTM with Reviewed-by: tag.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sat, Oct 10, 2026 at 02:09:53PM -0700, Shakeel Butt wrote:
> try_charge_memcg() does a lot. It charges the page counters, reclaims
> when a limit is hit, may call the OOM killer, and at the end it checks
> and enforces memory.high. Move the memory.high part into a new function,
> memcg_enforce_high(), so that try_charge_memcg() is shorter and the
> memory.high code is easier to read and change.
> 
> The code and its comments move as they are. The only difference is that
> the new function gets allow_spinning from gfp_mask itself.
> 
> No functional change.
> ---

Missing Signed-off-by: ?

Otherwise LGTM.
Reviewed-by: Harry Yoo (Meta) <harry@kernel.org>

-- 
Cheers,
Harry / Hyeonggon

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary: Responded positively to Harry's review, acknowledging the missing Signed-off-by: line and thanking him for his feedback.

Thanks for the review.

2026-10-12.patch_summary: This patch series cleans up memory.high enforcement in the Linux kernel by moving it out of try_charge_memcg() and using a worker for kernel threads and remote charges. The changes aim to improve performance and reduce delays caused by reclaiming and sleeping during charges.
